<RecipePage recipeId="retrieve-document-by-url">

<RecipeSection label="Problem">

A search result or chat citation gives you a document URL. To see the title, permalink, and extracted text for that one document, you call Glean's experimental document endpoints, then confirm the document ID in the response reads back the same document. The published TypeScript API client does not include these endpoints, so this quickstart calls the HTTP API and uses the official auth package for sign-in.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeCodeWalkthrough />

<RecipeArchitecture />

<RecipePrereqs />

<RecipeSteps />

<RecipeSection label="Keep the experimental header on every request">

This client sets X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on every request. Keep that header if you add a call. A 404 with the header usually means your Glean instance has not turned these endpoints on. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Request only documents:read">

OAuth login and the token provider use the documents:read scope. Do not add other scopes. If you create an API token instead, choose Read documents (documents:read). On the legacy token screen, choose DOCUMENTS.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Treat HTTP 404 as a failed command">

HTTP 404 exits non-zero and does not print Round-trip document_id matches. It usually means your Glean instance has not turned these endpoints on. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support, and share the Request ID. If the endpoints are on, a 404 usually means the document does not exist or you cannot access it. The batch command lists a missing document ID or URL under warnings and still exits 0.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Experimental endpoints">

These endpoints are experimental and can change. This client sends X-Glean-Include-Experimental: true on every request. If your Glean instance has not turned the endpoints on, you still get HTTP 404. Ask your Glean admin or Glean support. The published @gleanwork/api-client package has no methods for these endpoints. client.documents reads documents through a different API. Do not call it here.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Some documents cannot be retrieved">

A Gmail or Outlook search result or chat citation can show an ID that only works in that result. Pass the message URL instead of that ID. The URL can still return 404. Go links and federated search results cannot be retrieved. You only get documents you can open.

</RecipeSection>

<RecipeSection label="Content is extracted text, not the file">

include=CONTENT adds content.full_text_list. An empty list means Glean stored no extracted text. You still see the document. If Glean cannot read the text you asked for, the command fails instead of printing the document without content. The command prints a short preview, not every segment.

</RecipeSection>

<TakeItFurther>

- Pass --content when you need extracted text. include=CONTENT adds content.full_text_list. An empty list means Glean stored no extracted text. You still see the document. If Glean cannot read the text you asked for, the command fails.
- Use the batch recipe when you have many document IDs and URLs. Copy the document_id line this command prints and pass it to --id there. The batch prints documents Glean returns under results, and document IDs or URLs it does not return under warnings.
- Keep the document_id this command prints. The get-by-id call accepts that ID. For a Gmail or Outlook message, pass the message URL, not the ID from the search result or chat citation.

</TakeItFurther>
